text:
Detroit outshot Seattle 40 to 24, piled up 82 shot attempts to 53, and still lost by three goals. The Red Wings deserved to win this one 58 percent of the time, and a stretch of 3 minutes and 44 seconds in the second period is why they didn't. After William Wallinder gave Detroit a 2-1 lead at 4:00, Seattle answered with three goals before the eight-minute mark: Frederick Gaudreau at 4:39, Mackie Samoskevich at 6:59, and Gaudreau again at 7:44.

None of those chances was especially good. Gaudreau's goals carried 10 and 8 percent odds, Samoskevich's 20, and John Gibson let in five on 15 shots, roughly three more than the quality of those looks should have produced. Daniil Tarasov relieved him and was fine. Ben Meyers made it 5-2 at 14:05, and the game was effectively gone by the second intermission. Seattle's even-strength expected goals were only 2.3 against Detroit's 3.56, so the Kraken turned modest looks into a 6-3 win.

Philipp Grubauer made the lead stand, stopping 37 of 40 against 3.79 expected goals. Vince Dunn added a power-play goal in the third, and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård got one back late on a 52 percent chance. Gaudreau, Meyers (a goal and two assists) and Berkly Catton (a goal and an assist) were the stars for a Seattle team that wasn't the better side but was far sharper at finishing.
